Canopy browning and recovery were quantified using a 2010–2022 Sentinel-2 time series of Normalized Burn Ratio (NBR), which has been previously identified as the most effective spectral index for detecting drought-related declines in canopy greenness, and were validated with field-measured canopy health. Artificial neural networks were used to link NBR z-scores with climatic (precipitation, temperature, potential evapotranspiration), topographic (Topographic Wetness Index, aspect, slope), soil, and vegetation variables. Lagged and cumulative precipitation and temperature emerged as the dominant drivers of canopy browning, while recovery was influenced by potential evapotranspiration and temperature. Regional contrasts underscored the role of local climate, topography, and vegetation composition in shaping drought impacts and post-drought recovery trajectories.

rows.title: Multi-head attention driven aggregation-differentiation network for probabilistic groundwater depth forecasting and depth-stratified early warning: A multi-site efficient framework
rows.abstract: Accurate groundwater depth (GWD) forecasting is critical for sustainable water management, yet remains challenging due to the reliance on multi-source data and inadequate uncertainty-guided warning strategies. This study presents a Multi-Head Attention driven Aggregation-Differentiation Network (MHA-ADNet), a novel efficient framework that requires only historical GWD records for probabilistic multi-site forecasting. MHA-ADNet decouples the learning process into an aggregation module, which extracts shared temporal features across monitoring wells by multi-head attention, and parallel differentiation modules that capture site-specific characteristics, with integrated quantile regression for uncertainty assessment. Validated on data from 43 wells in Eastern China, the framework achieves superior performance across multi-step predictions (7-day R2 ≥ 0.89, 14-day R2 ≥ 0.85, 30-day R2 ≥ 0.72), consistently outperforming baseline models. It demonstrates higher reliability in deep inland aquifers and facilitates depth-stratified early warning strategies using prediction intervals. MHA-ADNet provides a practical tool for probabilistic groundwater forecasting and adaptive warnings, making it particularly valuable for management in data-scarce regions.

rows.title: Lessons learned from building Confluence: Cloud-based global river discharge estimation software for the SWOT satellite
rows.abstract: We present Confluence, a cloud-based workflow that produces river discharge products on demand by processing the entirety of NASA/CNES Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) mission hydrology data. Confluence integrates dozens of established science algorithms into a unified framework, leveraging cloud resources to meet demands for RAM, storage, and CPU time beyond the capacity of local clusters. Built on AWS Batch, Step Functions, and other AWS services, Confluence accesses input data from 15 sources in multiple formats, orchestrates algorithm processing, detects and recovers from failures, and reports on workflow states. It produced global SWOT discharge products in approximately 4.5 days at a cost of ∼$6000. Confluence's design includes a community of practice to guide development, with over 50 hydrologists contributing to results validation. This architecture, together with its community engagement model and cost-efficient execution strategies, offers a generalizable solution for science teams translating complex algorithms into operational cloud-based workflows.

rows.title: An independent-scheduling variables LPV model integral–delay–zero representation for open-channel: Development and applicability boundary identification
rows.abstract: Accurate modelling of open-channel systems remains challenging due to dynamic hydraulics and coupled boundary–disturbance interactions. Existing linear parameter-varying (LPV) models often rely on a single variable, limiting their ability to characterize coupled interactions, and lacking quantitative applicability criteria to assess model validity. This study develops an independent-scheduling variables LPV integral–delay–zero (ISV–LPV–IDZ) model, in which low-frequency parameters are governed by upstream discharge and downstream water-level, while high-frequency ones depend on disturbance amplitude and spectral center frequency. A boundary identification method informed by high-frequency response energy defines the model's applicability domain. Results demonstrate that ISV–LPV–IDZ model reduces the full-period RMSE by 83% and the steady-state error by 86% compared with LPV–ID model while maintaining boundary identification errors around 1 cm. High-frequency response energy is primarily governed by spectral center frequency and decreases by approximately 70%–95% as steady-state discharge increases from 80 m3/s to 150 m3/s.

rows.title: Building and managing local databases from Google Earth Engine with the geeLite R package
rows.abstract: Google Earth Engine (GEE) has substantially expanded the scope of geospatial analysis by providing access to petabyte-scale satellite imagery and geospatial data together with cloud-based computation. This accessibility enables researchers to study large-scale environmental and socio-economic processes with high spatial and temporal coverage. In recent years, numerous R packages have emerged to leverage GEE’s functionalities. However, constructing and managing complex spatio-temporal databases for continuous monitoring of remotely sensed data remains challenging and often requires advanced coding skills. To bridge this gap, we introduce the geeLite R package (available on CRAN), which supports the construction and updating of local databases for GEE-derived outputs, enabling users to track their evolution over time. By storing results in SQLite format — a serverless, self-contained database solution requiring no additional setup — geeLite simplifies data collection. It also streamlines conversion to native R formats and provides functions to aggregate and process the resulting databases for downstream analysis.

rows.title: Advancing geospatial data infrastructure in Dataverse via metadata automation, interactive tools and LLM case study
rows.abstract: In the era of big data and interdisciplinary research, the effective dissemination and reuse of geospatial data have become vital across various fields such as economics, biostatistics, epidemiology, environmental health, and sciences. This study investigates the challenges associated with managing geospatial data and presents the implementation of tools designed to address these challenges. We present an overview of the current state of geospatial data in a general-purpose research data repository Dataverse and outline a series of implemented advancements for improving the management and utilization of geospatial datasets. These advancements include building the capability to extract structured metadata automatically, enabling programmatic engagement with data assets, incorporating checklists, facilitating geospatial-specific searches, and providing previews of geographic dataset coverage. In this paper, we include two case studies. In the first, we evaluate the effectiveness of the automatic metadata extraction feature, part of our proposed advancements, using the large language model GPT-4 and find that the extracted metadata offers unique information, which is not typically provided by the user. In the second case study, we introduce the community of practice around climate-health data at Dataverse, coordinated through the CAFE Research Coordinating Center.

rows.title: Corrigendum to “Multi-objective optimization of nature-based solutions in urban stormwater management: A scoping review” [Environ. Model. Software 194 (2025) 106659]
A spatially hybrid hydrological modeling approach using subbasin-specific model structures
rows.abstract: Hydrological models adopting spatially consistent model structures are often ill-suited for complex application contexts with significant spatial heterogeneity. Although existing hydrological modeling frameworks support spatially varying lumped or semi-distributed conceptual structures, they face challenges in integrating distributed physically-based structures. This paper proposes a new spatially hybrid hydrological modeling approach combining compatible spatial units and simulation algorithms to construct distinct model structures for individual subbasins within a watershed, integrated through channel routing for watershed-scale simulation. Implemented within the open-source Spatially Explicit Integrated Modeling System (SEIMS), this approach was evaluated through a proof-of-concept case study using two distinct model structures: a lumped conceptual model for gently sloping subbasins and a fully-distributed semi-physically-based model for mountainous subbasins. Comparative experiments demonstrate that the hybrid model inherits both the strengths and limitations of its constituent structures, achieving a balanced performance improvement. This approach enhances modeling flexibility, advancing knowledge-driven intelligent modeling in spatially heterogeneous environments.

rows.title: An explainable machine learning framework coupled with the PLUS model for ecological resilience simulation and zoning under SSP-RCP scenarios: A case study in Eastern Jilin, China
rows.abstract: Interpretable modelling frameworks are increasingly needed to assess ecological resilience under global change. This study develops an integrated framework coupling the Patch-generating Land Use Simulation (PLUS) model with explainable machine learning (XGBoost-SHAP) to simulate and interpret spatiotemporal ecological resilience patterns based on a Resistance-Adaptability-Recovery (RAR) structure. Applied to eastern Jilin Province, China, it analyses resilience dynamics from 2000 to 2020 and projects conditions to 2035 under multiple SSP-RCP scenarios. Results show a persistent southeast-northwest resilience gradient, with higher resilience in forested uplands. Land-use intensity (LUI) is the dominant intrinsic driver, exhibiting a nonlinear threshold effect. Future projections indicate overall improvement by 2035, strongest under the sustainability-oriented SSP1-2.6 scenario, with dominant drivers shifting from land-use structure to climatic and topographic controls. This framework links resilience projection, driver attribution, and spatial differentiation, offering a methodological tool for resilience-oriented land-use planning under global change.

rows.title: SWAT-UQ: A platform for uncertainty analysis, calibration and optimization of SWAT models
rows.abstract: The Soil and Water Assessment Tool (SWAT) is widely used for watershed modelling and water resources management. However, robust SWAT applications often require comprehensive uncertainty analysis, calibration, and optimization, which necessitate the integration of various methods. These workflows typically involve thousands of model runs and the complex manipulation of distributed parameter files, posing challenges to operational feasibility and computational efficiency. This study presents SWAT-UQ, an open-source platform designed for the uncertainty analysis, calibration, and optimization of SWAT models. SWAT-UQ enables the flexible configuration of algorithms to address both uncertainty quantification and decision-oriented tasks. It features a queue-based distributed computing framework that dynamically schedules large ensembles of SWAT runs and intensive file operations. To accommodate diverse user groups, SWAT-UQ is provided as both a scriptable development package and a graphical interface for end-to-end workflows without the need for coding. Two case studies, involving model calibration and Best Management Practice (BMP) multi-objective optimization, demonstrate SWAT-UQ's workflow flexibility, computational efficiency, and accessibility.

rows.title: Improving spatial land-use and land-cover change simulations with machine learning: A Python adaptation of the CLUMondo model
rows.abstract: Simulating land-use and land-cover change (LULCC) is key for assessing sustainable land-management strategies. Traditional models often rely on logistic regressions (LR) to estimate land-use suitability, which are limited in modelling complex, nonlinear relationships. We present CLUinPy, a Python-based adaptation of CLUMondo allowing the integration of advanced machine learning (ML) methods for suitability modelling. Using Mato Grosso, Brazil, we apply ML to simulate LULCC from 2012 to 2022. We compared different suitability modelling approaches regarding statistical performance (AUC) and impact on land-use allocation (figure of merit – FOM). ML outperformed LR, with random forest showing higher predictive accuracy for suitability (AUC 0.95 vs. 0.82). For land allocation, XGBoost was most accurate (FOM 0.148 vs. 0.074). Model projections to 2040 indicated 14.5% less forest loss with XGBoost compared to LR, alongside smaller aboveground biomass declines (10.2% vs. 12.4%). CLUinPy demonstrates that ML integration enhances LULCC modelling accuracy and reproducibility, improving scenario reliability to inform decision-making.

rows.title: Mapping four decades of change: Deep learning and Google Earth Engine for annual LULC classification in semi-arid regions
rows.abstract: Reliable long-term land use and land cover (LULC) datasets remain scarce in semi-arid regions. This study proposes a scalable and transferable deep learning framework that leverages Landsat archives and Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) to generate a continuous annual LULC dataset from 1985 to 2025 in M'sila, Algeria, as a representative semi-arid case study. The framework incorporates an additional refinement step by integrating the Spectral Angle Mapper (SAM) to generate spectrally stable training samples. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework effectively captures complex spectral relationships, enabling the generation of the first temporally consistent annual LULC dataset spanning 40 years for the study area. Moreover, generalization tests conducted on a geographically similar region indicate satisfactory transferability, with some limitations arising from interactions between land cover patterns and varying geographic conditions. These results demonstrate the potential of deep learning with satellite data for generating robust long-term LULC datasets for environmental monitoring.

rows.title: Global sensitivity analysis workflows and rankings: A practical comparison for researchers
rows.abstract: Global sensitivity analysis (GSA) is a recommended step in the use of computer simulation models. GSA quantifies the relative importance of model inputs on outputs (Factor Ranking), identifies inputs that could be fixed, thus simplifying model calibration (Factor Fixing), and pinpoints areas for future data collection (Factor Prioritization). Given the wide variety of GSA methods, choosing between methods can be challenging. We provide a practitioner-focused guide for non-GSA experts that compares both widely and less commonly used GSA methods, discuss implementation and interpretation issues, and propose a workflow. We assess the degree of similarity in Factor Ranking based on a study of three simulators of differing complexity. A critical issue for all methods is specification of parameter ranges. Factor Rankings were generally quite similar based on Kendall’s W. Sobol’ first order and total sensitivity indices were easy to interpret and informative with regression trees providing additional insight into interactions.

rows.title: An intelligent decision support framework for generating flood control emergency plan using knowledge graph and fuzzy enhanced entity recognition model
rows.abstract: Scientific flood control emergency plans serve as the primary support for enhancing the efficiency of flood emergency management. This study proposes a hybrid entity recognition model based on Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM), Conditional Random Fields (CRF), and the Ratcliff/Obershelp algorithm. A basin flood control knowledge graph is established, and a dynamic emergency plan generation framework based on hybrid reasoning is proposed. The case study indicated that the entity recognition model achieves a precision of 0.985, a recall of 0.990, and an F1-score of 0.987. The framework-generated plan reaches an 0.810 similarity with the 2023 historical flood control emergency plan of Tongchuan city of Shaanxi Province of China. This research offers an efficient entity recognition solution and an intelligent decision-making framework for the field of basin flood control, which can help to improve the precision of flood control management and emergency response efficiency.

rows.title: Untethered from earthly constraints: A spatial seven-day ahead machine-learning forest fuel moisture forecasting system, independent of real-time sensor networks
rows.abstract: Dead fuel moisture content (DFMC) critically influences wildfire behaviour, and its modelling underpins many fire management decision support systems. Recent modelling advances have enabled accurate forecast of point-scale fuel moisture, but their reliance on continuous real-time sensor functionality creates operational vulnerabilities when sensors may fail. Maintaining sensor networks across large, remote domains is costly and unreliable. Therefore, we developed a spatially continuous DFMC forecast system that eliminates real-time sensor dependency by replacing sensor initialisation with remotely sensed and modelled proxies for landscape fuel moisture states. Using 23,354 site-day observations from 27 forested sites in Victoria, Australia, our machine learning model produces 7-day ahead sub-canopy DFMC forecasts with median RMSE of 11.5% and 12.8% for day 1 and 7. The approach delivers reliable spatial forecasts across forested landscapes without sensor-dependent vulnerabilities, representing a significant advancement in operational fire risk management by providing comprehensive coverage for wildfire suppression planning and prescribed burning.

rows.title: Explainable sequence-aware deep learning based decadal shoreline modelling in the Southern Baltic until 2050
rows.abstract: Understanding future shoreline evolution is fundamental to developing adaptive coastal management strategies under climate change scenarios. This study analyzes the Southern Baltic Sea's ∼37-km stretch comprising Usedom and Wolin islands, where sandy coastlines face intensifying erosion threats under rising anthropogenic and climatic pressures. We introduce an explainable Long Short-Term Memory Recurrent Neural Network (LSTM-RNN) framework designed to bridge the gap between Deep Learning (DL) performance and physical interpretability in decadal forecasting. The results show that the best model achieves a Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) of 10.40 m, Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 7.13 m, and R-squared (R2) of 0.55. Deep SHapley Additive exPlanation (DeepSHAP) attribution reveals that erosion is driven by the compound interaction of sea-level rise (SLR), storm surges, and extreme waves. This transferable framework represents a significant methodological contribution, enhancing regional early-warning systems and providing a robust, “white-box” approach for Baltic Sea's operational coastal management.

rows.title: Ridiculously simple data-driven air pollution interpolation method
rows.abstract: Air pollution interpolation is crucial for civil management: it is used to transform limited sensor data into comprehensive pollution maps. Various methods, including deterministic, geostatistical, and Machine Learning (ML)-based techniques have been utilized for this purpose. Deterministic methods rely on mathematical rules for estimation, whereas geostatistical techniques are based on spatial correlations. ML leverages historical data for predictions. Each method has limitations: deterministic methods do not adequately model environmental complexity, geostatistical methods struggle with small-scale areas, and ML depends heavily on data availability. On the other hand, air pollution simulators based on physicochemical dispersion models capture intricate pollution dispersion patterns, yet running them at high resolution for continuous interpolation is often computationally demanding. Recent advancements in ML offer a complementary pathway by leveraging simulated data to enable rapid, real-time interpolation. This study introduces an air pollution interpolation approach combining simulated air-dispersion patterns through an educated machine that includes machine learning and environmental modeling that considers boundaries, pollution sources, obstacles, wind dynamics, and topography. Specifically, we present a combined ML-based linear regression model designed to infer dense concentration maps from a sensor array using state-of-the-art simulation methods. We dub this the Ridiculously Simple data-driven air pollution Interpolation Method (RSIM). The RSIM method was evaluated on both synthetic and real-life-based simulation models. The synthetic scenarios included an industrial area with point pollution sources and an urban road surrounded by buildings simulating traffic-related pollution. The real-world environment consisted of sensor data and simulations from Antwerp, Belgium. The results indicate that this method outperforms standard techniques for reconstructing dense pollution maps from sparse sensing, and demonstrates significant promise for other real-world applications.

rows.title: A lightweight deepwater oxygen model for investigating lake responses to future climate
rows.abstract: Climate-driven deepwater deoxygenation is a growing global concern for lake ecosystems. We developed a simple 1-D deepwater oxygen profile model to understand the underlying physical mechanisms and to quantify the required climate-adaptive interventions. It was applied to Lake Erken, Sweden, using hydrodynamic forcing under three Representative Concentration Pathway (RCP) scenarios. From 2020 to 2099, the annual anoxic factor (the number of days when the anoxic sediment area equals the lake surface area) projections show non-significant trends under RCP2.6, while increasing by 0.4 and 0.6 days year−1 decade−1 under RCP6.0 and RCP8.5, respectively. This climate-driven future deoxygenation, consistent across multiple oxygen metrics, mainly stems from prolonged stratification. To mitigate climate impacts by 2100, oxygen depletion rates, as a proxy for eutrophication, would need to be reduced by approximately 9–13%, 20–24% and 26–35% under RCP2.6, RCP6.0 and RCP8.5, respectively. This data-efficient framework can be applied to physically-dominated, seasonally stratified lakes.

rows.title: Extended Hydrofabric: A standardized geospatial database for reproducible water management modeling in the United States
rows.abstract: The large-scale application of Water Management Models (WMMs) is limited by fragmented, non-standardized water management data, and a lack of integration with hydrologic models. To address this gap, we developed automated, reproducible workflows that extend the United States’ reference hydrofabric to explicitly include water management infrastructure such as reservoirs and diversion points while populating a relational database containing operational and administrative records. Piloted across the entire Upper Colorado River Basin (UCRB), this work integrates 1318 diversions and 37 major reservoirs using persistent identifiers to ensure interoperability with existing national hydrologic models including the National Hydrologic Model and the National Water Model. The resulting contributions are, first, a basin-scale Extended Hydrofabric data product for the UCRB, directly useable for constructing WMMs and coupling with hydrologic models, and second, designs and workflows that enable generation of Extended Hydrofabric for other managed basins and provide a foundation for future conterminous United States-scale applications.

rows.title: AutoICE: An automated tool for estimating ice thickness and volume of glaciers in mountain regions
rows.abstract: AutoICE is an automated tool for estimating glacier ice thickness and volume in mountainous regions using remote sensing inputs such as DEMs, glacier outlines, cross-sections, surface velocities, and temperature data. It implements the newly developed Velocity-based Ice thiCkness Estimation (VoICE) model, which applies the shallow ice approximation and ice flow laws to estimate thickness without requiring field measurements. Validation exercise on four glaciers located in High Mountain Asia showed good agreement, although error variability was observed depending on the glacier characteristics. Comparison with in-situ measurements confirmed that the outputs are physically consistent. Likewise, comparisons with existing velocity-based models demonstrated that the proposed VoICE model achieved lower errors and minimal bias in the distributed ice thickness distribution and bed profiles. Additionally, scalability of the AutoICE was demonstrated using 2023 data from the Miyar Basin, western Himalayas. The tool successfully modelled ice thickness, volume, associated uncertainties, and bed topography for 54 glaciers, estimating a total ice volume of 14.20 ± 4.13 km3. Simulations revealed that the processing time ranged from just 30 min to a few hours per glacier, depending on glacier size, on standard computing system, making it practical for both individual glacier studies and large regional-scale applications.

rows.title: A framework approach for analyzing water transformation characteristics of typical watersheds in arid zones during irrigation periods
rows.abstract: This study investigated the Ebinur Lake Basin in arid inland China, focusing on the spatiotemporal dynamics of hydrogen and oxygen isotopes to elucidate water recharge mechanisms and transformation processes. A two-endmember mixing model was used to quantify the respective contributions of precipitation and snowmelt, while the SHAP (Shapley Additive Explanations) framework was employed to identify key environmental drivers. The results indicate that snowmelt account for an average of 58% of total surface and groundwater recharge, with the remaining 42% originating from precipitation. A progressive monthly decline in surface–groundwater exchange rates was observed, reflecting seasonal hydrological variations. Climate variability remains the primary control on basin-scale isotope dynamics, whereas LUCC and irrigation-related disturbance can impose strong sub-basin modulation. These findings provide a scientific foundation for sustainable water resource management in arid regions.

rows.title: Extensive model evaluation for seasonal and spatial dynamics of dissolved oxygen in SWAT+
rows.abstract: Dissolved oxygen (DO) is a critical indicator of aquatic ecosystem health, but multidecadal trends show a general decline in DO concentrations in riverine ecosystems, highlighting the need to better understand the driving dynamics and improve predictions. This study presents the first implementation of dissolved oxygen (DO) dynamics in SWAT+ (SWAT + DO). A rich dataset of spatially high resolution observed DO data is used to investigate modelled and observed differences in seasonal and spatial DO dynamics related to stream temperature and hydrological conditions. The spatial model performance was improved by introducing a spatially distributed formulation of the K2,20 parameter and achieved a KGE of 0.73 on a daily resolution without further calibration. The influence of streamflow and stream temperature on DO has strong seasonal and spatial differences. With these findings our study highlights the strengths and limitations of a process-based ecohydrological model, depending on the scale that it is applied on.

rows.title: Overcoming barriers to reproducibility in geoscientific data analysis: Challenges and practical implementation strategies
rows.abstract: Reproducibility is a cornerstone of the scientific method, yet it remains elusive in many domains of contemporary research, including the geosciences. In this Perspective, we examine reproducibility in the context of computational workflows for geospatial analyses. Building on established frameworks, we disentangle key dimensions — methodological, results, and inferential reproducibility — and identify critical barriers, including irreproducibility arising from obscurity, obfuscation, and uncontrollable conditions. We argue that enhancing reproducibility in geoscientific research requires both cultural transformation and practical, domain-specific interventions. Our focus lies on methodological and computational reproducibility, with particular attention to challenges posed by spatial data structures, diverse data sources and infrastructures, and the integration of statistical and machine-learning methods. We outline actionable guidance across the research workflow, including data governance, analysis design and documentation, code development, and long-term accessibility. Emphasis is placed on the use of open-source software, script-based automation, version control, and the adoption of FAIR principles to support findability, accessibility, interoperability, and reusability of data and code. Our aim is to provide a structured synthesis that supports reproducible and transparent geospatial research. By implementing even incremental improvements, researchers can strengthen the robustness, transparency, and reuse potential of their scientific contributions.

rows.title: Portable multi-GPU urban flood modelling via MPI-OpenACC: evaluating acceleration, scaling, and workload-per-GPU
rows.abstract: We present a multi-GPU implementation of the physics-based 2D urban flood model (H12) utilising MPI-OpenACC, demonstrating significant reductions in runtime for high-resolution, city-scale, and large-basin simulations. Applied to grids ranging from 1 to 20 m across two basins (downtown Portland, Oregon, USA; downstream Han River, South Korea), the multi-GPU configuration achieved a speedup of approximately 710 × over a serial baseline and approximately 30 × over a 144 core CPU-hybrid run. This advancement renders metre-scale, city-wide scenarios and extensive domains computationally feasible. Our findings provide practical guidance for determining optimal GPU counts based on workload per device; while exact thresholds vary with problem size (spatial coverage and resolution) and system interconnect, the underlying principle aids in aligning domains with available accelerators. The directive-based MPI-OpenACC design maintains a unified code base across CPU and GPU execution, thereby supporting portability and operational use.

rows.title: Editorial Board
Emulating the Global Change Analysis Model with deep learning: An energy sector case study
rows.abstract: The Global Change Analysis Model (GCAM) simulates the evolution of the coupled Earth-human system, but its complexity makes large ensemble studies for uncertainty exploration computationally expensive. We develop an efficient deep-learning emulator that approximates GCAM outputs. This allows us to estimate the model response across many more parameter settings than feasible with full model runs, enabling faster exploration and improved scenario discovery. The deep learning-based emulator is trained on an existing large ensemble with outputs spanning the water, land, and energy sectors. We evaluate performance across multiple training set sizes. Results show high predictive accuracy across 22,528 outputs, even when trained on substantially fewer samples than the original ensemble. This efficiency allows the design of large ensembles that more efficiently explore the GCAM input–output space. To our knowledge, this is the first successful multi-sector dynamic model emulator for scenario discovery, offering a simple, adaptable machine-learning approach for exploratory modeling studies.

rows.title: Hydrological climate change impact assessment in high latitudes: are bucket-type models up to the task?
rows.abstract: Accurate future flow projections necessitate hydrological models suitable for such a purpose. However, there are no formal guidelines on model selection. We here evaluate the suitability of 29 commonly used bucket-type models for climate change impact studies across 50 high-latitude catchments. Model performance is represented by various indicators and the percentage of catchments with well-reproduced hydrological signatures. Models are grouped according to their structural attributes, and performance among the groups is compared to identify key features. Models generally reproduce well mean flows, 30-day maxima and runoff seasonality, but perform less reliably under low-flow conditions. Best-performing models feature balanced complexity with non-linear soil- and routing parameterisations and a limited number of parameters. Complexity of the snow routine does not noticeably influence overall model performance, as opposed to the efficiency in low flows. These findings contribute to good modelling practice by supporting systematic model selection for climate change impact studies in high latitudes.

rows.title: Editorial Board
An interpretable AutoML–SHAP approach for rapid urban pluvial flooding prediction
rows.abstract: Intensified urban pluvial flood risks highlight the urgent need for accurate, efficient, and transparent forecasting tools. However, the black-box nature of current machine learning surrogates limits their interpretability regarding key drivers. In this context, this study proposes a novel framework that integrates Automated Machine Learning (AutoML), SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), and Generalized Additive Models (GAM). Using Beijing's Shijingshan District as a case study, the AutoML-optimized XGBoost generalizes well to unseen rainstorms, achieving a 2000-fold speedup over MIKE FLOOD. The integrated SHAP–GAM analysis reveals nonlinear responses that align with hydrological expectations, reinforcing the credibility of the learned decision behavior. Depth-stratified analysis further shows stage-specific dynamics: elevation, topographic wetness index, and manhole density form a core driver set (contributing over 43% across depth bins), with their hierarchy reorganizing as severity increases. Overall, by integrating predictive power with interpretability, the proposed framework enables rapid and transparent urban flood forecasting and management.

rows.title: MiniGeoSolver: Enhancing small language models for autonomous geospatial tool sequences generation through progressive strategy
rows.abstract: Using tool sequences for tackling geospatial tasks is a challenge. While large language models (LLMs) excel in generating these sequences, their computational costs restrict deployment. Small language models (SLMs) offer an alternative. Traditional approaches directly train SLMs to generate tool sequences often fail due to entangled reasoning paths and excessive load. Therefore, we propose MiniGeoSolver, a progressive training strategy designed to enhance SLMs. To establish a clear reasoning trajectory, MiniGeoSolver breaks down the complex sequences generation process into two stages. First, it constructs a symbolic framework to determine required tools. Then, it aligns detailed execution with this framework to generate accurate workflows. We fine-tune Gemma-2-2B using a split dataset and use an evaluation dataset to assess task-solving ability. Results demonstrate that our model outperforms GPT-4 by 22.7% and Gemini 1.5 Pro by 17.2%. Additionally, our progressive strategy realizes 9.5% higher accuracy than data generated without a progressive design.

rows.title: Dynamic integration of water quality simulation into Pywr
rows.abstract: The dynamic relationship between water quantity and quality has been neglected in water resources models. This study dynamically integrated simple water quality processes into Pywr to allow water quality to inform water allocation. To demonstrate, Pywr-WQ is applied to the highly human-modified Grootdraai Dam catchment in southern Africa. Pywr-WQ simulations of Total Dissolved Solids (TDS) and various nutrients were generally representative of variations in observed water quality in the Grootdraai Dam. Water quality thresholds for water abstraction were applied to the Grootdraai Dam, with the results showing that Pywr-WQ dynamically ‘switched off’ the abstraction when these thresholds were exceeded. This study confirms the viability of dynamically adding water quality simulation to Pywr. This can aid in more realistic estimations of water yield considering water quality constraints. Given the flexibility of Pywr, more complex rules between water quantity and quality can be implemented.

rows.title: A 3D shallow translational landslide susceptibility model accounting for side resistance and vegetation roots
rows.abstract: Uniform rainfall infiltration and infinite slope stability models are computationally efficient for large-scale landslide susceptibility mapping but overlook three-dimensional (3D) effects from complex topography, side resistance, and spatial-temporal variability in rainfall and soil properties. While 3D limit equilibrium models address these issues, they are computationally intensive over large regions. This study introduces a Three-Dimensional Translational Slide (3DTS) model for simulating rainfall-induced shallow landslides. The 3DTS model integrates the generalized Green-Ampt infiltration approach for non-uniform rainfall with a corrected 3D Janbu method that accounts for side resistance and vegetation root reinforcement. Each digital elevation model (DEM) cell is treated as a soil column, aggregated to form slip surfaces. Validation against 3D Bishop and finite element methods demonstrates the model's accuracy and efficiency. A case study of landslides in 2011 at Kvam, Norway, investigates the influence of slip surface geometry, rainfall conditions, side resistance, and vegetation roots on landslide prediction.

rows.title: Provena 2.0: Enabling provenance in operational modelling of reef restoration and adaptation interventions in the Great Barrier Reef
rows.abstract: As environmental modelling outputs increasingly inform decisions, careful management of their provenance supports transparency and scientific integrity. Provena is a system designed to capture this provenance and provide traceability across modelling activities, from datasets and models through to the organisations and people involved. Originally developed for the Reef Restoration and Adaptation Program (RRAP) to support the Modelling and Decision Support (MDS) subprogram, Provena underpins the MDS information system and facilitates the management of ecological and environmental model outputs and collaboration across teams. Operational use of the system has revealed new needs, including tracking studies that span multiple modelling activities and managing versions of data over time. These insights have driven the development of Provena 2.0. In this paper, we outline these new features, including tools to register studies linking related model runs and mechanisms for versioning datasets and registry items to track changes over time. Together, these features improve traceability and defensibility of modelling artefacts and support reproducibility.

rows.title: A novel hybrid fine-tuning method for supercharging deep learning model development for hydrological prediction
rows.abstract: This study proposes a novel hybrid method that substantially accelerates and improves deep learning (DL) model development for streamflow prediction. The method leverages a combination of a long short-term memory (LSTM) network and random forests. A hybrid encoder-decoder model is designed using a pre-trained LSTM to extract temporal features, followed by a random forest decoder for streamflow prediction. Our method was tested on 421 catchments in the continental United States and 324 in Germany. The hybrid method has several benefits. First, it shows competitive performance compared to regional LSTM models (e.g., 6.66% improvement in the median in Nash-Sutcliffe Efficiency (NSE)) when trained with less data. Second, it is more efficient and robust than training LSTMs on each catchment individually (∼14x faster) and achieves superior accuracy, and third, it is much less computationally expensive than regular fine-tuning (i.e., feasible on a CPU-based workstation).

rows.title: Knowledge-guided hybrid AI framework for GRACE data reconstruction and generalization in South Asia: A spatiotemporal perspective
rows.abstract: The GRACE (-FO) missions captured crucial gravity-based signals of Earth's terrestrial mass shifts, but an 11-month gap and isolated data lapses disrupted its continuity, complicating its robust reconstruction. To address this, we propose a knowledge-guided hybrid framework integrating domain-informed feature engineering with multiscale nonlinear learning. We developed two hybrid models, Coupled Empirical Orthogonal Function–Random Forest (CEOF-RF) and Temporally Segmented- Spline Extreme Gradient Boosting (TS-SplineX), and evaluated them alongside standalone models via a Monte Carlo-based remove-and-restore framework. The CEOF-RF combines orthogonal function-based spatial mode extraction with nonlinear learning, allowing physically coherent and multivariate-aware reconstructions. In contrast, TS-SplineX employs wavelet-spline interpolation followed by XGBoost, capturing local anomalies, seasonal discontinuities, and nonlinear dependencies. TS-SplineX with ReliefF-derived features showed consistent performance (RMSE: 0.225 cm; r > 0.97; NSE >0.94), without adding artefactual trends. This study offers an adaptable and interpretable reconstruction framework for satellite data assimilation and multi-region hydrological analysis in climate-vulnerable regions.

rows.title: A novel adaptive time-scale decomposition fused LSTM-transformer framework (ATSD-LT) for TCWV prediction
rows.abstract: Total column water vapor (TCWV) is vital for the water cycle, precipitation, and extreme weather events. This study proposes a novel adaptive time-scale decomposition fused LSTM-Transformer framework (ATSD-LT). ATSD employs gradient-optimized filters to resolve sequences into trends and multi-scale fluctuations, suppressing aliasing and frequency leakage. Through heterogeneous ensemble modeling, LSTM extracts trend evolution while Transformer captures global long-range spatiotemporal correlations. Results yield superior performance, particularly in spring and summer (R2 of 0.959 and 0.967, respectively). Compared to Autoformer, Informer, Transformer, and LSTM, ATSD-LT demonstrates more significant gains in winter (improving R2 by ∼18%–55% and reducing MAE by 64%–76%). Ablation tests confirm the proposed ATSD-LT framework achieves a total 79.4% reduction in summer MAE, while feature weighting provides an additional 12.3% goodness-of-fit gain. Spatial mapping reproduces tropical highs (e.g., Amazon Basin) and high-latitude lows (e.g., northern North America); cross- and site-validation further confirm framework robustness. ATSD-LT effectively supports global climate monitoring and water management.

rows.title: Optimizing canopy cover evaluation: A machine learning approach using LiDAR data
rows.abstract: This article introduces a comprehensive framework that uses LiDAR data and machine learning techniques to predict a range of biophysical variables. The framework is tested explicitly on Canopy Cover. The methodology combines optimized feature engineering, selection, and scalable parallel processing to ensure both accuracy and computational efficiency. The study demonstrates the efficacy of AI-CanopyMapper in accurately predicting canopy cover. The full model achieved a mean absolute error (MAE) of 6.47% and an R2 of 0.88. In contrast, the partial model, trained with only 1.3% of the available data, reached a MAE of approximately 15%, demonstrating strong generalization capabilities even under data-limited conditions. These results confirm that AI-CanopyMapper offers a fast, scalable, and data-efficient framework compared to traditional methods, highlighting its potential applications in forest management and environmental monitoring.

rows.title: RiverSTICH: Sewing together 3D rivers from only a few loose threads of transect data
rows.abstract: With the widespread application of 2D hydrodynamic models, river corridor topo-bathymetric data has become a constraint. Many global landscape settings remain unsuitable for modern topo-bathymetric data acquisition methods or there are insufficient resources to deploy them, leaving only traditional relative river cross-sectional surveys. This study aims to improve representation of variability in channel width and bed elevation in the interpolation of sparse surveys. We introduce RiverSTICH (River Survey Transect Interpolation to reconstruct 3D Channels), a Python-based preprocessing tool designed to assimilate sparse cross-sectional surveys and translate them into inputs suitable for continuous 3D river corridor generation using River Builder. We demonstrate that RiverSTICH-derived river corridor terrains can achieve comparable hydraulic performance to HEC-RAS RAS Mapper given only relative cross-sectional surveys, distance along channel, and minimal feature labelling (thalweg and banks). Future work could explore the effects of different cross-section shapes, surveying schemes, and longitudinal channel variability on topo-bathymetric reconstruction.

rows.title: Data assimilation-based correction of flood forecasts in a large-scale river network: A case study of the Pearl River Basin
rows.abstract: Accurate prediction of water levels is imperative for navigation safety, flood mitigation, and infrastructure management; however, predictive capability is often compromised by rapidly evolving hydrological conditions and boundary uncertainties. To address these challenges, this study develops a data assimilation framework coupling a one-dimensional hydrodynamic river network model with the Ensemble Kalman Filter (EnKF). The proposed framework dynamically identifies Manning's coefficients under uncertain boundary inputs while ensuring numerical stability and hydraulic consistency. Validated in the Pearl River Basin, the system assimilates in-situ water-level observations to generate forecasts across multiple lead times (1–24 h) over a continuous 30-day (720 h) simulation. Results demonstrate that the EnKF-based assimilation effectively mitigates systematic biases and sustains stable forecasting performance, achieving an average Nash–Sutcliffe Efficiency (NSE) of 0.85 across 33 stations. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework for water-level forecasting under complex boundary conditions within the examined case study.

rows.title: A coupled stormwater-power model for the simulation of cascading infrastructure failures: An application in Phoenix, AZ
rows.abstract: Urban infrastructure is typically designed in isolation, neglecting system interdependencies and the effects of spatiotemporal variability of climate forcings across systems. Here, these limitations are addressed by developing the PSI-Cascade Python-based framework, which simulates cascading failures from power to stormwater infrastructure under high-resolution space-time wind gust and precipitation forcings. PSI-Cascade couples open-source, spatially explicit stormwater and power infrastructure models and represents cascading failures on stormwater pumping stations caused by wind-induced power outages through user-defined fragility curves, linking wind gusts with the transmission line failure probability. Using Phoenix, AZ as a case study, it is shown that PSI-Cascade adequately captures the spatiotemporal variability of documented street flooding, particularly around pumping stations that likely stopped operating due to wind-triggered power outages. The case study also highlighted the importance of parameterizing the fragility curves based on local failures. The PSI-Cascade framework is a valuable tool for increasing urban flood resilience.

rows.title: Converging human intelligence with AI systems to advance flood evacuation decision
rows.abstract: The powers that artificial intelligence (AI) have developed are impressive, with recent success in leveraging human expertise at various stages of model development. However, AI can only attain its full potential when it actively teams with humans to co-create solutions. This study introduces a Human-AI Convergence (HAC) system for flood evacuation decision-making. The goal is to develop a unique, computationally effective HAC system for flood evacuation decision-making that integrates AI with transportation geospatial data, a river hydraulic model, and human data from X. The HAC system is smartly designed to forecast flood stage levels using AI across the US Geological Survey gauging stations, visualized in a web-based Google Earth architecture. HAC has been tested in the Lowcountry of South Carolina, where previous floods caused considerable damage to the transportation networks and increased traffic on evacuation routes. The system stands to advance the frontier of human-AI collaboration for real-time flood management.

rows.title: Makurhini: An R package for comprehensive analysis of landscape fragmentation and connectivity
rows.abstract: Habitat fragmentation and climate change threaten biodiversity, emphasizing the need for landscape connectivity to help species access habitat resources and track ongoing shifts in suitable areas. Given limited conservation funds and land-use conflicts, the efficient prioritization of connectivity measures is essential. To that end, we developed the Makurhini R package, an open-source tool for systematically calculating key fragmentation and connectivity metrics. Makurhini provides integrated analytical capabilities and efficiently processes large datasets, including parallel processing, allowing parameterization for different species and landscape contexts. Key features include characterizing links using Euclidean, least-cost, and circuit theory approaches; calculating the Probability of Connectivity, Equivalent Connected Area, and Protected Connected indicators, among other metrics; and ranking nodes and links by their contribution to connectivity. Case studies in Mexico, Colombia, and Spain demonstrate its applicability. Makurhini provides a robust framework to deliver ecologically and policy-relevant connectivity and fragmentation metrics for conservation and restoration in fragmented landscapes.

rows.title: Probabilistic modelling of atmosphere–surface coupling with a copula Bayesian network
rows.abstract: Land–atmosphere coupling is an important process for correctly modelling near-surface temperature profiles, but it involves various uncertainties due to subgrid-scale processes, such as turbulent fluxes or unresolved surface heterogeneities, suggesting a probabilistic modelling approach. We develop a copula Bayesian network (CBN) to interpolate temperature profiles, acting as alternative to T2m-diagnostics used in numerical weather prediction (NWP) systems. The new CBN results in (1) a reduction of the warm bias inherent to NWP predictions of wintertime stable boundary layers allowing cold temperature extremes to be better represented, and (2) consideration of uncertainty associated with subgrid-scale spatial variability. The use of CBNs combines the advantages of uncertainty propagation inherent to Bayesian networks with the ability to model complex dependence structures between random variables through copulas. By combining insights from copula modelling and information entropy, criteria for the applicability of CBNs in the further development of parameterizations in NWP models are derived.

rows.title: Editorial Board
Water–sediment multi-objective synergetic scheduling of reservoirs considering reservoir–river coupling: a case study of the Middle and Lower Yellow River
rows.abstract: Sedimentation in sediment-laden rivers degrades reservoir and channel capacities. To achieve coordinated reservoir-river sediment regulation while meeting multiple water demands, this study develops a synergetics-based water-sediment multi-objective scheduling model considering reservoir-river coupling in the Middle and Lower Yellow River. Pareto trade-off analysis examines competition and synergy among subsystems. Changes in sediment transport targets and sensitivity analyses reveal the system's response characteristics. Results indicate: (1) Sustaining channel sediment transport capacity requires a bankfull discharge above 4000 m3/s; (2) The model achieves an annual mean sediment delivery to the sea of 1.992 × 108 t, and the reservoir-river coupled sediment transport subsystem competes with the other subsystems; (3) Changing sediment release requirements shifts reservoir operation trajectories and alters ecological, water-supply, and hydropower benefits; (4) The system is sensitive to inflow and sediment variability, and a 50% inflow reduction markedly weakens multi-objective performance. The results provide insights for sediment-laden cascade reservoir management.

rows.title: Optimization of wastewater treatment plant considering the uncertainty of treatment process effectiveness
rows.abstract: Effective wastewater treatment has gained significant momentum due to limited global clean water access. Although many models for wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) exist, the integration of byproduct and waste management systems remains limited, potentially incurring increased costs and pollutant emissions. Moreover, existing optimization approaches inadequately capture the uncertainty of the treatment process effectiveness, which compromises the system's ability to satisfy quality requirements. Thus, a target-oriented robust optimization (TORO) model for a hybrid WWTP and byproduct disposal system (BDS) that minimizes cost and environmental impact is developed. The case study implemented validates the model's ability to balance objective trade-offs while underscoring the importance of the process effectiveness on the system's performance. TORO allows decision makers to set targets and select solutions for managing hybrid WWTP-BDS systems based on their varying risk-appetites. These solutions show increased stability, demonstrating the potential of the proposed framework to enhance sustainability and robustness of wastewater management.

rows.title: Interpretable residual-informed hybrid physics-informed machine learning framework for runoff prediction in a typical karst basin in southwest China
rows.abstract: Accurate runoff prediction is essential for water resource management. This study developed a residual-informed hybrid physics-informed machine learning (PIML) framework that integrates Xin'anjiang (XAJ) hydrological model, Seasonal-Trend decomposition using Loess (STL), Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD), Convolutional Neural Network–Long Short-Term Memory (CNN–LSTM) hybrid architecture, and SHapley Additive Explanations (SHAP)—and applies it to a representative karst basin in Southwest China. When evaluated for runoff prediction, the framework achieves a Nash–Sutcliffe Efficiency (NSE) of 0.93 and reduces peak prediction error to 8.14%, outperforming standalone models. SHAP-based interpretability analysis reveals soil moisture, cumulative atmospheric humidity, and surface energy balance as key drivers. When coupled with a reservoir operation model, the proposed framework produces more accurate inflow estimates, thereby enhancing hydropower generation performance under challenging hydrological conditions. Overall, the proposed framework enhances runoff prediction accuracy, demonstrates strong engineering applicability, and provides transferable solutions for water resources management in complex karst basins.

rows.title: An interactive web-based framework for scenario-driven dust storm simulation and mitigation analysis
rows.abstract: Evaluating long-term dust storm mitigation strategies such as terrain modification remains challenging due to fragmented analytical workflows and the absence of integrated tools for iterative, scenario-driven analysis. This paper presents an interactive web-based framework for scenario-driven analysis of dust storm variability and mitigation strategies. The framework integrates terrain editing, HPC-based simulation management, and comparative visualization within a unified environment, enabling domain scientists to draw terrain modification polygons directly on a geographic map, automatically update simulation input files, submit and monitor simulations asynchronously, and compare results through linked visualization views. A case study focused on the Arabian Peninsula showcases the framework’s ability to reveal new insights into dust storm variability and assess the effectiveness of mitigation strategies. Evaluation with five independent domain experts yields a mean System Usability Scale (SUS) score of 82.0, and all participants confirmed the efficiency of the integrated workflow. This work represents a shift from passive data visualization to an active, hypothesis-driven research paradigm to support complex environmental decision-making.

rows.title: Deep learning in modeling urban growth dynamics: a systematic literature review
rows.abstract: As far as the authors are aware, this study provides the first-of-its-kind comprehensive literature review based on the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) approach to examine Deep Learning (DL) applications in modeling urban growth dynamics. Analyzing 2674 papers published between 2010 and 2025, we observe a substantial rise in DL-based research in recent years. DL architectures are categorized into Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), Deep Feedforward Neural Networks (DFNNs), Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), and Transformer Networks. These approaches are further classified into non-hybrid and hybrid models integrating Cellular Automata (CA). Findings reveal that non-hybrid methods span all architectures, while hybrid applications are confined to CNNs, RNNs, and DFNNs. Despite advances in encoder-decoder networks and channel attention mechanisms, challenges persist, including limited integration of demographic and socioeconomic data, extensive training data requirements, and prolonged computational time for hyperparameter optimization. Lastly, we identify seven future directions, emphasizing feature learning, temporal flexibility, and public perception modeling. This review guides urban planners in selecting appropriate DL architectures for specific urban contexts, optimizing data integration strategies, and balancing model complexity with computational constraints, thereby fostering sustainable urban development and advancing knowledge of urban growth dynamics.

rows.title: Investigating the impacts of parameter fixing on the performance of a spatially distributed water quality model with an adaptive emulation approach
rows.abstract: Fixing model parameters deemed unimportant is a common practice in solving inverse problems, one that is often determined by Global Sensitivity Analysis. Yet little attention has been paid to understanding the variations in the model parameter-objective function (ObF) map caused by parameter fixing (PF), and the accompanying implications for model calibration and uncertainty assessment. We develop an approach to explore variations induced by PF in the parameter-ObF map of a spatially-distributed water quality model (the GBR Dynamic SedNet model), using an adaptive Gaussian Process emulator to enhance the computational efficiency. This study shows that characteristics of an ObF can be substantially altered by PF in ways that are quantified by a range of metrics. The approach warrants further application to other case study catchments and hydrologic models, and indeed to over-parameterized models more widely, to improve the use of parameter fixing and as a contributor to good modeling practice.

rows.title: Non-stationary multi-covariate flood frequency analysis with TRUE: A tool for time-varying return levels of univariate extremes
rows.abstract: Conventional stationary models fail to account for temporal variability and dynamic factors influencing flood regimes, limiting their effectiveness in flood risk prediction. This study introduces a Non-Stationary Multi-Covariate Flood Frequency Analysis (NSMCFFA) framework to improve flood risk modeling under changing climatic conditions. Applied to five gauging stations in the Narmada River Basin (NRB), India, the framework integrates climatic, ecological, and anthropogenic covariates. We also present TRUE (Time-varying Return level for Univariate Extremes), a MATLAB-based GUI that allows user-defined covariates and employs the Deviance Information Criterion (DIC) for optimal model selection. Bayesian inference is used to estimate model parameters and return levels. Results reveal spatial variability in covariate influence: Mohgaon is climate-driven, while Barmanghat, Handia, Garudeshwar, and Mandleshwar are shaped by both climatic and anthropogenic factors. Findings show that non-stationary models better represent flood return levels than stationary ones, establishing NSMCFFA as a robust framework for flood management in the NRB.

rows.title: Interaction of sustainable development goals from an environmental perspective
rows.abstract: Understanding the interrelationships among Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) is essential for addressing interconnected environmental challenges. This study examines the complex links among SDG 13 (Climate Action), SDG 14 (Life Below Water), and SDG 15 (Life on Land) using a systems-based approach. We develop a hybrid analytical framework that integrates Tree-Augmented Bayesian Networks (BN-TAN), Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM), and Importance–Performance Map Analysis (IPMA) to identify structural, probabilistic, and performance-based interactions across all SDGs. Using global SDG indicator data, the analysis uncovers influential pathways, leverage points, and performance gaps that shape environmental outcomes. Results highlight SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production) as the most critical driver across all three environmental goals and reveal notable trade-offs, including negative associations between SDG 3 and SDGs 13 and 15. By combining quantitative modeling with policy-relevant interpretation, the study offers actionable insights to support integrated environmental governance.

rows.title: The expanded spatial lag of exogenous model and RShiny-based web application for rainfall prediction
rows.abstract: This study proposes the Expanded Spatial Lag of Exogenous model, which captures the spatial autocorrelation of exogenous variables and extends to surrounding areas. The exogenous variables considered are air temperature, humidity, and surface pressure. Moran's Index test confirms the appropriateness of applying these variables. Then, the model is abstracted as an RShiny-based web application, allowing users to interact. The model and web application are then implemented using climate data from Java Island, the region with the highest hydrometeorological risk in Indonesia. The data are sourced from NASA POWER, the large-scale climate database. Due to the large volume of data, the Data Analytics Life Cycle is utilized for data discovery, preparation, model planning, construction, evaluation, and deployment. The proposed model empirically achieves a Mean Absolute Percentage Error of 4.22% in-sample and 3.53% out-of-sample. This study provides a tool to predict the rainfall in some areas (spatial prediction), supporting hydrometeorological risk assessments.

rows.title: Heat-Wave Prediction via Joint Regression and Classification with a Bayesian Deep Bidirectional LSTM Model
rows.abstract: Extreme heat-waves are severe climate hazards, threatening public health, ecosystems, and urban infrastructure. Accurate and uncertainty-aware prediction is vital for early warning, risk management, and climate adaptation. This study introduces a Bayesian Deep Bidirectional LSTM (BiLSTM) framework that unifies regression and classification for heat-wave prediction, enabling both maximum temperature forecasting and reliable event detection. The framework integrates Bayesian inference, bidirectional memory, and extreme value analysis for event labeling, while class imbalance is addressed using a Dirichlet Extended SMOTE method to generate distribution-aware synthetic samples, enhancing robustness under abnormal heat-wave patterns. Hyperparameters are optimized via Bayesian optimization, improving predictive stability. Results show strong performance with balanced accuracy of 0.93, F1-score of 0.8868, RMSE of 0.1829, R2 = 0.89, and reliable uncertainty quantification (95% PICP = 93.31%). The proposed framework offers a scalable and reliable result for operational temperature forecasting with heat-wave detection, implication for climate planning and decision making. For practical deployment, a “Heat Wave Prediction App” was developed based on the proposed model provides seven-day forecasts and heat-wave detection.

rows.title: Transparent and reproducible crop model calibration using exclusively public data: Improving phenology and yield predictions in APSIMx
rows.abstract: Reproducible APSIMx calibration studies using exclusively public data remain limited, yet such transparency is essential for reliable crop modeling. This study demonstrates that publicly available climate, soil, and observational datasets can improve yield and phenology predictions for winter wheat, silage maize, winter oilseed rape, and spring barley across two contrasting German pedoclimatic regions. We developed a stepwise calibration workflow using the croptimizR R package, optimizing phenology parameters before yield-related parameters. Calibration reduced phenology and yield RMSE by 1.9–14.3 days and 10–167 g m−2 across crops. However, improvements at one site occasionally coincided with deterioration at the other, reflecting inherent trade-offs when calibrating across contrasting environments. While public data introduce uncertainties limiting interannual variability capture, the resulting generic parameters provide robust regional estimates for Central European applications, demonstrating the potential of public datasets for transparent crop model calibration. All workflows are publicly available.

rows.title: A data-driven framework for Korean extreme rainfall: Leveraging adversarial generation of extreme samples
rows.abstract: This study refines the adversarial generation of extreme samples (ExGAN) framework to generate extreme rainfall scenarios over the Korean Peninsula based on 5 km gridded observations (2014–2023). Methodological refinements include separating typhoon and monsoon data, applying log transformation to stabilize heavy-tailed distributions, using data-driven mean residual life plots for objective generalized Pareto distribution thresholding, modifying conditional sampling to correspond to physically meaningful return periods, and improving Fréchet inception distance (FID) evaluation by defining reference distributions from autoencoder-derived features of the test set. Performance is evaluated using FID, mean absolute percentage error (MAPE), and reconstruction loss. For 100-year typhoon events, the FID, MAPE, and reconstruction loss are 1.18±0.65, 14.19%, and 0.0921, respectively. Semivariogram analysis confirms that the generated extremes preserve spatial dependence patterns consistent with observations. This work presents a transferable methodological advancement for generative modeling in complex climates and a practical tool for climate risk assessment in Korea.

rows.title: The emerging application of partial least squares structural equation modelling in ecological research: An introductory overview
rows.abstract: The need to better understand the complex relationships between variables in Ecological Research (ER) has led to adopting advanced methodologies, such as Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM). PLS-SEM is well-established in several fields but is only beginning to gain traction in Ecological Research. To ensure best practices, ER studies must rigorously evaluate their use of PLS-SEM. Consequently, this study briefly introduces PLS-SEM and reviews its application in 149 ER studies conducted between 2017 and 2024, analysing 381 models. Compared to established guidelines, the review reveals significant opportunities for improvement in areas including sample size determination, measurement model specification, model assessment, reporting, handling data heterogeneity, accounting for variable interactions, addressing nonlinearity, and exploring alternative plausible models. Finally, this study envisions the growing integration of machine learning techniques with PLS-SEM and proposes a framework for their conjunctive application in ER.

rows.title: Artificial intelligence with earth observations provides continuous streamflow data across varying wildfire recurrence and recovery scenarios
rows.abstract: Wildfires continue to alter watershed hydrology globally. Numerous studies have analyzed post-fire hydrology through before- and after-fire comparisons—often focusing on a single fire event. This has led to a significant gap in research, where continuous, daily streamflow data are needed to capture both the short- and long-term effects of recurring fires. Our study, for the first time, demonstrates how Artificial Intelligence (AI) through Machine Learning/Deep Learning (ML/DL) models can fill this gap by harnessing Earth Observations of burn severity, fire radiative power, and burn dates alongside traditional watershed attributes and drought indicators. We present a highly efficient DL model based on the Long Short-term Memory (LSTM) algorithm that is both reproducible and generalizable across multiple fire-affected watersheds in the western United States. Despite watersheds’ diverse climate conditions and markedly different hydrologic characteristics, the model consistently achieves strong performance, with Kling Gupta Efficiency ranging between 0.7 and 0.9. Our primary contribution is testing the model at a daily time-scale to model three distinct fire scenarios: no significant fire history yet the occurrence of a large fire, a longer return interval and no-fire period between phases of recurring fires, and frequent and repeated fire activity. We further investigate whether a relatively simple ML model such as Support Vector Machine (SVM) can achieve comparable accuracy in capturing these complex post-fire scenarios. By offering this fully open-source, generalizable AI solution powered by Earth Observations, newer and better modeling tools can provide post-fire daily streamflow data—a step in the right direction to safeguard water supply reliability and support watershed management across fire-prone regions worldwide.

rows.title: Decision support systems for urban water scarcity: Gaps, barriers and pathways to integrate nature-based solutions - A systematic review
rows.abstract: Urban water scarcity is intensifying due to rapid urbanization, climate change, and ageing infrastructure. In this context, Nature-based Solutions (NbS) offer potential to address urban water challenges by restoring ecological functions and delivering multiple co-benefits, yet their systematic integration into Decision Support Systems (DSS) remains limited. This study systematically reviews 50 peer-reviewed publications (2015–2025) to evaluate current knowledge, methodological gaps, and opportunities to integrate NbS within DSS for urban water scarcity. Results reveal that most DSS are predominantly focused on gray infrastructure, with limited capacity to model or evaluate NbS. Key barriers include technical and modeling constraints, governance and institutional fragmentation, socio-economic and participatory challenges, and geographical research imbalances. Identified opportunities include hybrid modeling approaches, sensor-supported monitoring methods, and application of digital twin technologies. In response to the identified gaps, the study proposes a conceptual decision-support framework integrating hydroinformatics, socio-ecological analysis, and stakeholder participation to strengthen urban water resilience.

rows.title: An open-source GIS user interface for the TARGET climate model in the Urban Multi-scale Environmental Predictor (UMEP) tool
rows.abstract: The Air-temperature Response to Green/blue-infrastructure Evaluation Tool (TARGET) is a compact urban climate model designed to predict intra-urban temperatures and assess city cooling strategies. Until now, the lack of a user interface has limited its broader adoption. This study presents an open-source interface for TARGET, integrated within the Urban Multi-scale Environmental Predictor (UMEP) tool in QGIS. The interface supports a complete workflow, including input data preparation, simulation, and output visualisation. Its applicability is demonstrated through a case study in Zurich, Switzerland, where it identified thermal hotspots and quantified the cooling benefits of targeted interventions. By lowering technical barriers, UMEP-TARGET enhances the accessibility of physically based urban temperature modelling for both the scientific community and practitioners, supporting evidence-based planning for climate adaptation.

rows.title: Coupled estimation of root zone soil moisture and soil hydraulic parameters with reduced-adjoint variational data assimilation using near-surface soil moisture observations
rows.abstract: Accurate estimation of root-zone soil moisture and soil hydraulic parameters is essential for simulating water and energy fluxes, optimizing agricultural water use, and improving drought and flood forecasts. These quantities are difficult to measure directly but can be inferred by combining hydrologic models with remotely sensed near-surface soil moisture. Variational data assimilation (VDA) provides a rigorous framework for this purpose but often requires computationally expensive full-model adjoints. The Reduced-Adjoint Variational Data Assimilation (RA-VDA) framework overcomes this limitation by integrating Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD) model reduction with a reduced-order adjoint, making it model-agnostic and computationally efficient. This study extends RA-VDA to coupled state–parameter estimation and evaluates its robustness under structural, initial condition, and forcing uncertainties using HYDRUS-1D. Results show that RA-VDA maintains accuracy while remaining computationally tractable and demonstrating strong resilience to errors, establishing its potential for large-scale environmental modeling without requiring full-model adjoint codes. Importantly, RA-VDA's model-agnostic design makes it directly applicable to any existing hydrologic or land surface model without internal code modification, offering a practical and scalable path toward satellite-driven soil moisture and hydraulic parameter estimation at regional and global scales.

rows.title: New perspectives in high-resolution 3D modelling and simulation of atmospheric dispersion on giant urban areas to support emergency preparedness and response
rows.abstract: Accidental or malevolent atmospheric releases are feared as they pose a serious threat to human health and the environment. We first outline the gap between advanced atmospheric transport and dispersion (AT&D) models developed by the scientific community, and the oversimplified models present in decision-support systems (DSSs). We then describe a modelling system compromising between the detailed resolution of the AT&D equations and the fast delivery of operational results. We illustrate this approach through the “EMERGENCIES Méditerranée” project and demonstrate the possibility of producing micrometeorological forecasts that are ready to be used in emergencies, as well as meter-scale dispersion simulations, on demand and within accelerated time. The study areas cover megacities along the French Mediterranean coast. The calculations, carried out on powerful but affordable computing resources, represent a world first. Finally, we discuss the overall concept of the system developed, arguing that it could revolutionize preparedness and response to emergency situations.

rows.title: Corrigendum to “AutoICE: An automated tool for estimating ice thickness and volume of glaciers in mountain regions” [Environ. Modell. Software, 200 (2026) 106953]
Weight-level integration of SHAP-interpreted machine learning and AHP for flood susceptibility mapping in a semi-arid region
rows.abstract: Flood susceptibility mapping is critical for urban planning in semi-arid regions exposed to high-intensity seasonal rainfall and rapid urban growth. Conventional approaches often involve subjective weighting and limited interpretability. This study proposes a GIS-based weight-level integration approach linking interpretable machine learning with the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP). Four tree-based models were trained using standard and spatial cross-validation; SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) quantified factor contributions, enabling recalibration of expert-derived weights. CatBoost demonstrated the strongest generalization, achieving 85.19% standard and 73.30% spatial accuracy. ROC-AUC analysis showed that AHP + SHAP and standalone AHP attained the highest discriminative performance (AUC = 0.964), outperforming conventional map-level integration (AUC = 0.958) and standalone CatBoost (AUC = 0.859). The framework proved robust to weight perturbations, unlike map-level integration which produces polarized patterns. Weight-level integration yields balanced spatial distributions and reduces false alarms, providing a transparent scheme for data-constrained urban contexts to support informed environmental decision-making.

rows.title: AMAformer: Dynamic and accurate forecasting of water quality in aquaculture with adaptive multi-kernel decomposition and attention
rows.abstract: Accurate water-quality prediction is essential for sustainable aquaculture. However, multivariate time series are highly coupled, nonstationary, and multiscale, posing challenges for long-term modeling. This study proposes AMAformer, a Transformer-based model for aquaculture forecasting. First, Adaptive Multi-kernel Temporal Decomposition separates trend and seasonal components to mitigate baseline drift. Second, Adaptive fractional Fourier-domain spectral Attention uses learnable fractional Fourier projections to capture nonstationary spectral peaks and cross-frequency dependencies. Third, Adaptive Channel–Temporal Hybrid Gating integrates channel-wise and temporal attention for modeling cross-variable and long-range dependencies. Experiments on six searanch datasets demonstrate that AMAformer outperforms eight baselines, reducing the mean absolute error (MAE) and root mean square error (RMSE) by 33.67% and 26.49% relative to the best-performing baseline, and improving coefficient of determination (R2) and Kling–Gupta Efficiency (KGE) by 9.22% and 4.56%, respectively.
