Near-river groundwater dynamics (0–5 km) were mainly linked to river stage and runoff with an approximately 1-month lag, while high suspended sediment concentration may reduce river-aquifer exchange efficiency. Far-river dynamics (10–15 km) were dominated by agricultural water consumption (maximum contribution: −48.77%).

rows.title: Precipitation downscaling for climate characterization with scarce data using transfer learning
rows.abstract: High-resolution precipitation data is essential for applications such as agriculture, infrastructure planning, and climate risk assessment, particularly in regions with complex terrain. Conventional climate datasets, including satellite and reanalysis products, are often too coarse to capture local variability. Downscaling techniques refine these data, but traditional dynamical methods are computationally intensive, and statistical methods require long-term observations that are often unavailable. We present a deep learning-based downscaling framework using transfer learning. A base model is pre-trained on large datasets and then fine-tuned to regions with limited local data, reducing the need for extensive weather station networks. Applied to Ecuador, the method produces accurate long-term precipitation estimates with only a few years of observations. This approach is flexible, extendable to other climate variables, and suitable for downscaling future climate projections, demonstrating the potential of transfer learning to improve the accessibility and quality of high-resolution climate information in data-scarce, topographically complex regions.

rows.title: Spatio-temporal dynamics of biochar application as a climate tool in European agriculture: Economic insights
rows.abstract: Biochar application on agricultural land is promoted for its high permanence as a carbon sink. This study examines the spatiotemporal dynamics and economic net benefits of biochar sequestration in EU agricultural soils from 2020 to 2050. A discrete time dynamic economic optimization model, spatially disaggregated across 26 EU member states, evaluates trade-offs between using agricultural residues for biochar, bioenergy, direct soil incorporation, and cover crops. Results show that biochar will become economically viable within the next decade, with optimal carbon stocks reaching 0.6–6.8 tonnes per hectare by 2050. Countries with abundant biomass benefit most due to economies of scale and lower transport costs. By 2050, optimal carbon sequestration yields a net present value of about 212 billion euro, including 36 billion from biochar. Sensitivity analysis underscores the influence of carbon pricing, production costs, and regional biomass supply. Biochar thus offers a cost-effective, regionally variable mitigation option for the EU.

rows.title: SPEIChanges: A framework for assessing climate-change-driven shifts in drought frequency using the standardized precipitation evapotranspiration index
rows.abstract: Developing methods based on widely used probability-based indices to quantify how changing climate patterns alter drought occurrence is crucial. In this study, we developed SPEIChanges, an open-source framework designed to quantify how shifts in the central tendency and dispersion of the precipitation-atmospheric evaporative demand (P-AED) distribution affect drought likelihood of occurrence. Simulation results indicated that the Bayesian Information Criterion should be used within the algorithm. We assessed SPEIChanges performance using observed data and climate projections representing contrasting global conditions. The results showed that SPEIChanges characterizes shifts in expected P-AED values and changes in drought frequency. The method explicitly identifies whether these shifts are driven by changes in central tendency, dispersion, or both features. Notably, it detects and quantifies in probabilistic terms changes in drought frequency even when the widely used Mann-Kendall test fails to detect significant trends.

rows.title: Stepwise Clustered Ensemble (SCE): An R package for interpretable and robust regression in environmental modeling
rows.abstract: We present Stepwise Clustered Ensemble (SCE), an open-source R package for regression and inference designed to address key limitations of traditional random forest models. SCE replaces impurity splitting with a likelihood-based criterion using Wilks' Λ statistic and adds a node-merging step to prevent superfluous partitions. This statistically rigorous construction enhances parsimony and model generalization. The package is fully open-source and designed to integrate seamlessly into reproducible environmental modelling workflows, facilitating transparency and collaboration. The predictors selected by SCE transfer effectively to Random Forest model in the evaluated case studies, improving its performance and offering a practical route to feature selection. Through large-scale environmental applications in hydrology and air-quality modeling, SCE demonstrates strong predictive performance and interpretability while helping reduce overfitting and improve robustness to noisy environmental conditions. By integrating these innovations into an R package, SCE provides researchers with a robust, interpretable, and transferable framework for modeling complex environmental systems.

rows.title: Review on information entropy tools and applications for water system management
rows.abstract: Information entropy tools are increasingly used to quantify uncertainty, dependence and information transfer in water system management (WSM), but proliferating indices make applications difficult to compare. This paper reviewed entropy-related WSM studies in the Web of Science Collection. The search string (“information entropy” OR “mutual information” OR “transfer entropy” OR “maximum entropy” OR “entropy weight method” OR “sample entropy” OR “water quality entropy”) AND “water” yielded 6039 unique records; 5645 records published during 1981-2025 were analyzed, and 2890 WSM-relevant papers were selected by title/abstract/source screening and classified by water body and management scenario. We synthesize univariate uncertainty, multivariate dependence, entropy-weighting and optimization methods across data analysis, modelling, forecasting/risk assessment, water-quality analysis and source identification in different waterbodies. The review provides a scenario-oriented taxonomy to help users select appropriate indices and improve reproducibility and practical precision in entropy-based WSM, leading future directions in the era of big data and digital water.

rows.title: Individual tree mortality segmentation using a multi-task deep learning network and high-resolution aerial imagery
rows.abstract: Accurate mapping of individual tree mortality is critical for assessing forest carbon loss, yet dead trees in aerial imagery often appear scattered, irregular, and blurred, causing high omission rates and low precision for conventional semantic segmentation models. To solve this, we propose TreeMortSeg, a tree mortality segmentation network based on multi-task learning. Structure-aware and edge-aware auxiliary learning tasks are introduced to enhance the spatial structure representation and boundary localization of dead trees. These tasks provide effective spatial geometry and contour priors for the primary segmentation task, thereby reducing omission errors and improving segmentation precision. On the TreeFinder dataset, TreeMortSeg achieved the best dead tree F1-score (66.29%) and IoU (49.57%), outperforming the second-best model (DeepLabV3+) by 6.9 and 7.3 percentage points, respectively. Furthermore, it demonstrated strong robustness across diverse forest conditions and superior cross-regional generalizability. This research supports precise large-scale tree mortality mapping and reliable forest carbon loss assessment.

rows.title: Runoff simulation in a typical karst basin based on a Robust Dynamic Merging Algorithm for multi-source satellite precipitation and an improved Xin'anjiang hydrological model
rows.abstract: Precipitation uncertainty and complex generation processes hinder karst runoff simulation. We developed an integrated modeling framework combining the Robust Dynamic Merging Algorithm (RDMA) with the improved Xin'anjiang (KXAJ) model and evaluated it in Chengbi River Basin. RDMA dynamically merges five satellite precipitation products to generate robust forcing; KXAJ couples saturation-excess and infiltration-excess runoff mechanisms. The merged product (RDMAP) outperforms the best single-source product, improving KGE by 10.96% and reducing MAE by 34.83%. During validation, the framework improves NSE by 5.56% and decreases RMSE by 7.48%, with KXAJ consistently outperforming XAJ. Error attribution shows that precipitation input error contributes the least, confirming RDMA's effectiveness in enhancing temporal consistency, while interaction error dominates, highlighting the need for synergistic improvements in precipitation estimation and model structure. Multi-source uncertainty analysis confirms that KXAJ maintains stable performance and RDMA is insensitive to hyperparameter fluctuations and observational noise, demonstrating strong structural robustness for data-scarce karst basins.

rows.title: PM2.5 concentration prediction method based on laplacian-enhanced multi-pooling spatio-temporal self-attention
rows.abstract: Rapid urbanization exacerbates air pollution and endangers public health and economy. Accurate short-term PM2.5 prediction supports pollution control, policy-making and regional environmental governance. Driven by emissions, regional transport and meteorology, PM2.5 exhibits complex nonlinear spatiotemporal patterns. Existing models suffer defects in graph construction, spatiotemporal fusion and long-term temporal modeling. This work presents LGMPST, a spatiotemporal graph network integrating Laplacian probabilistic attention, graph-convolutional up-down mapping and multi-perspective pooling. Tested on 36 Beijing monitoring stations, LGMPST surpasses LSTM, AirFormer, STiTransformer and other advanced baselines. Seasonal comparison, multi-station tests, pollution-stratified evaluation and ablation studies validate its performance. Cross-regional experiments over Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei and Guangzhou further confirm generalizability for refined air-quality forecasting and joint governance.

rows.title: FIALab: an application for analyzing, mapping, and modeling forest attributes from the U.S. forest inventory and analysis database
rows.abstract: The U.S. Forest Inventory and Analysis (FIA) database provides comprehensive forest information on composition, structure, biomass, growth, removals, mortality, and disturbance. However, its complex data structure and design-based estimation framework can limit use by individuals without programming, database, or survey-estimation expertise. We developed FIALab, a free, cross-platform desktop application that provides an interactive environment for FIA data analysis without requiring software installation or coding. Seven modules support plot-level analysis of forest structure, composition, and biomass, point mapping of plot attributes, wall-to-wall interpolation, tree growth and allometry, forest health and disturbance assessment, climate-data acquisition and climate-forest analysis, and design-based forest carbon estimation. We demonstrate FIALab using statewide FIA data from Maine, USA, and evaluate broader applicability with data from Georgia. FIALab integrates data processing, statistical estimation, visualization, and spatial analysis, thereby reducing technical barriers and expanding the use of FIA data in forest management, research, education, and resource planning.

rows.title: Advancing urban flood modeling: A scalable, interoperable and reproducible high-resolution modeling framework and workflow
rows.abstract: Urban flooding is a growing issue worldwide, requiring high-fidelity, physics-based distributed models to capture flood dynamics at localized scales. Such modeling requires high-resolution spatial (e.g., ≤5m) and temporal data, resulting in substantial computational demands. In addition, hydrodynamic modeling tools, although based on similar physical principles, often require tool-specific data processing, resulting in fragmented data pipelines and workflows that limits scalability and interoperability. We present a scalable, interoperable, and reproducible framework for high-resolution 2D hydrodynamic urban flood modeling using a rain-on-grid approach with publicly available datasets. The framework integrates algorithms for data processing, model setup, and simulation execution, and is validated across watersheds and supports local and cloud computing environments. Case studies in Atlanta, Phoenix, Copenhagen, and Cape Town demonstrate scalability across geographic contexts and spatial resolutions, and interoperability across different hydrodynamic modeling platforms. This can further support infrastructure planning, emergency response, risk assessment, and development of physics informed machine learning models.

rows.title: A consensus-based framework for urban flood risk assessment under DEM uncertainty
rows.abstract: Digital Elevation Models (DEMs) are a major source of uncertainty in urban flood simulations. This study develops a consensus framework for urban flood risk assessment under DEM uncertainty in densely built-up central Shanghai. Five global DEMs drove TELEMAC-2D simulations under 50- and 100-year rainfall scenarios. A Risk Consensus Index (RCI) was introduced to quantify spatial agreement and identify stable risk zones. DEM suitability was evaluated using historical waterlogging detection, spatial consistency, and uncertainty characterization. Results reveal clear DEM-dependent differences, with Copernicus (COP) DEM producing the largest proportion of high-risk areas. Stable risk zones account for 11.52%–14.39% of the study area and represent priority areas for flood-risk management. Functionally, under the modelling conditions and scenarios adopted in this study, the five DEMs exhibit distinct expansive, sensitive, robust, and conservative risk-identification patterns. The framework supports DEM selection and reliable flood risk identification where high-resolution terrain data are unavailable.

rows.title: Sustainability-oriented data architecture for urban mobility: An integrated evaluation framework
rows.abstract: Urban mobility decarbonization is not only a technical challenge but also a governance issue, as fragmented data infrastructures across public agencies often constrain coordinated climate action. Despite increasing investments in smart mobility initiatives, many urban information systems remain poorly integrated, limiting data quality, interoperability, and institutional decision-making capacity. This study develops a sustainability-oriented data architecture for urban mobility carbon management, grounded in TOGAF and ISO/IEC 25012 principles. Rather than proposing a new environmental modeling, prediction, or optimization methodology, the study focuses on the data architecture and governance mechanisms required to operationalize such analyses within urban institutions. The proposed architecture integrates heterogeneous datasets from mobility, energy, and environmental domains while embedding governance and sustainability considerations throughout the data lifecycle. To assess its effectiveness, an integrated evaluation framework is applied, comprising the Conceptual Alignment Index (CAI), Conceptual Maturity Index (CMI), Resilience Readiness Index (RRI), and Sustainability Readiness Index (SRI). The results indicate strong conceptual coherence, architectural maturity, and resilience across alternative future scenarios, validated by an independent expert panel comprising academic and government practitioner evaluators, with aggregate scores of CAI 89.39%, CMI 58.50%, RRI 74.64%, and SRI 73.12%. A representative demonstration scenario using operational traffic and emission data from Bandung City further illustrates the practical applicability of the proposed framework within a real institutional context. Beyond technical performance, the findings highlight how integrated data infrastructures can enhance inter-agency coordination, analytical transparency, and evidence-based policymaking in urban mobility governance. This study contributes an integrated evaluation model that links architectural design, institutional alignment, and sustainability readiness, offering a transferable reference for cities seeking to strengthen digital infrastructures in support of long-term decarbonization transitions.

rows.title: QDataMap: An open-source plugin for automated multi-domain thematic mapping across administrative scales
rows.abstract: This study presents QGIS Data Mapping (QDataMap), an open-source QGIS plugin that encodes an expert-validated cartographic specification into a reproducible, parameterised workflow for the automated spatial representation of statistical data. Rather than extending layout flexibility, QDataMap constrains it by design through a fixed layout template defined via structured consultation with domain and risk-assessment experts. The template is exposed through 34 core parameters, of which only three must be set by the user, ensuring that visual differences between any two maps in a series reflect differences in the data rather than in authoring decisions. The specification was developed to support European Food Safety Authority and Joint Research Centre plant health assessments under EU Regulation 2016/2031, where the resulting map series served as mandatory input to Expert Knowledge Elicitation sessions. To assess how far this specification has been made transferable from GIS specialists to domain experts, we additionally report a descriptive accounting of interaction cost, expressed as the number of discrete user operations required to produce a map series, as supporting context for this transferability claim. Producing the reference specification through the manual QGIS workflow requires 239 user operations for the first map and an additional 81 operations for each subsequent map. In contrast, QDataMap requires a single configuration followed by one execution, eliminating any additional user operations for subsequent maps. Two applications illustrate the workflow in a complementary way. The first focuses on the batch production of EU-27 agricultural statistics at the regional level (NUTS2), while the second explores its use across diverse thematic and spatial contexts. This second application combines rapid mapping of socio-economic indicators across Africa with colour-vision-deficiency palettes, while extending the workflow to a global climate data at a different administrative level, highlighting the versatility of QDataMap across thematic domains, geographic extents, and spatial scales.

rows.title: Modeling Anthropocene systems of systems: Comparing system dynamics and hetero-functional graph theory
rows.abstract: Anthropocene Earth systems require advanced modeling to address complex, multi-domain societal challenges. This paper evaluates Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) coupled with Hetero-functional Graph Theory (HFGT) as an extension to traditional System Dynamics (SD). A formalized rubric compares both methodologies across graphical modularity, boundary explicitness, and computational scalability. Using a Mono Lake case study, numerical results demonstrate strict analytical equivalence across three multi-scenario perturbations, yielding normalized Root Mean Square Errors (nRMSE) below 1.15% and Pearson correlation coefficients (r) exceeding 0.999. Building on this baseline equivalence, we hypothesize that the explicit structural rigor and mathematical scaffolding of MBSE-HFGT will overcome scalability limitations to effectively model highly coupled, large-scale Anthropocene Systems of Systems—a theoretical advantage to be tested in forthcoming work.

rows.title: Knowledge-guided graph time-series modelling for regional carbon emission prediction and decision support: An integrated assessment of carbon peaking pathways in Guangxi
rows.abstract: Accurate long-horizon carbon-emission forecasting requires models that capture inter-city dependence, remain robust under recursive prediction, and separate model outputs from policy targets. This study develops a Knowledge-Guided Graph Time-Series (KG-GraphTS) framework for 14 prefecture-level cities in Guangxi, China, using a 2000–2024 panel of socioeconomic, energy, industrial, demographic, remote-sensing, and climate variables. Secondary-industry GDP is incorporated both as a predictor and as structural knowledge for an economic-knowledge graph combining economic gravity, industrial-structure similarity, and geographical proximity. The model integrates graph convolution, a two-layer GRU, city-specific autoregressive residual learning, City-Specific Bias, and soft knowledge-guided regularization. A leakage-controlled chronological design is used for training, recursive validation, and held-out testing, while future emissions are projected under Baseline, Low-Carbon, High-Carbon, and Carbon-Neutrality-oriented scenarios without imposing terminal policy targets. KG-GraphTS achieves R2 = 0.9900 and RMSE = 2.1846 Mt under rolling evaluation and retains R2 = 0.9679 and RMSE = 3.9085 Mt under fixed-origin recursive testing. Under the Carbon-Neutrality-oriented scenario, emissions peak at 455.77 Mt in 2034 and decline to 165.90 Mt by 2060, a 63.6% reduction, yet all cities peak after 2030. Under the Baseline scenario, all cities reach Alert by 2030 and cumulative emissions exceed the Carbon-Neutral reference budget by 15.46 Gt CO2. These results support robust target-independent forecasting and transparent scenario-based decision support with explicit uncertainty and pathway diagnostics.

rows.title: An effective constraints handling method for medium- to long-term scheduling of water transfer projects under various hydrological scenarios
rows.abstract: Medium- and long-term scheduling for inter-basin water transfer projects is a high-dimensional, multi-constraint optimization problem. Existing solution methods are constrained by the mathematical properties of the scheduling model and computational efficiency, failing to meet the practical engineering needs. Therefore, based on the simulation–optimization approach (SIM) and analysis of the over-capacity flow (OF) relationships, this study proposes a constraints handling algorithm (OF-SIM) comprised of over-capacity flow traceability, over-capacity flow reduction, and dynamic boundary adaptation. OF-SIM is validated on the Yangtze-to-Huai Water Transfer Project scheduling model, which minimizes water deficit and surplus water across wet, normal and dry years. Results show average reductions (pooled standard deviations) of 98.49 million m3 (1.2 million) in water deficit, 114.64 million m3 (1.49 million) in surplus water, and 20.61 s in runtime across all scenarios compared to the alternate projection correction algorithm and forward-reverse simulation.

rows.title: Transforming multimodal data into decision assets: A vision-language model for ecological data using cross-modal alignment
rows.abstract: Environmental monitoring in complex rangeland ecosystems relies on human evaluation to navigate environmental shifts. Local community knowledge is important for guiding herd mobility decisions within pastoral systems that use rangeland ecosystems. Currently, human-based scouting considers factors like rangeland location, season, and plant composition to make decisions based on traditional knowledge. However, climate change impact makes rangeland monitoring more complex by reducing the predictability of vegetation availability, species composition, access, and seasonal grazing patterns. To address this, there is a demand to automate rangeland assessment to help sustainable management. We present a novel human-augmented ecological assessment framework that formalizes local community knowledge into a scalable, knowledge-aware AI system through a multimodal Mixture of Experts (MoE) architecture with bidirectional cross-attention mechanism. This model is fed by a multimodal dataset from sub-Saharan African rangelands collected mainly via a mobile app where stakeholders encode decision-making parameters. This architecture helps the disambiguation of visual features by grounding them in seasonal metadata, in which seasonal linguistic is designed to guide the model to prioritize site specific phenological patterns over undifferentiated spectral greenness. By employing a MoE layer to manage ecological data variability, our learning model uses community knowledge to override deceptive visual cues and improves rangeland quality classification over unimodal and standard fusion baselines. These results suggest that routing data through human-centric priors can improve rangeland monitoring.

rows.title: Explainable AI as a diagnostic tool for analyzing spatiotemporal variability in simulated groundwater recharge: Application to a semi-arid river basin
rows.abstract: Groundwater recharge is a vital component for water budget and water availability assessments but is challenging to measure due to its complex dynamics and subsurface occurrence. Process-based modeling tools are often used to simulate recharge. Analyzing the numerous, interacting factors that control recharge is time consuming and computationally expensive. In this study, we develop machine learning (ML) models that predict recharge and use explainable AI (XAI) as a diagnostic tool to understand the drivers of groundwater recharge, capture critical threshold values, and identify high recharge zones. ML models are trained and tested using calibrated SWAT+ simulated recharge values as the response variable. Two ML models are developed: (i) a surrogate model that captures the physics from the SWAT+ simulator by utilizing selected model inputs with a directly comparable definition of distributed parameter values; and (ii) a stand-alone predictor that utilizes commonly available open-source data to predict recharge and has annual temporal and 500 m spatial resolution for the period of 2002 – 2015. The study is implemented in the semi-arid Lower Arkansas river basin in Colorado, USA which contains an alluvial aquifer that is used for agricultural irrigation. Both the surrogate and stand-alone models demonstrated high predictive accuracy with NSE values of 0.98 and 0.91, respectively, when evaluated against test data. Explainable AI assessments show that the simulated groundwater recharge increases significantly when precipitation exceeds approximately 500 mm/year. Irrigation return flow is also identified as a major source of recharge where cultivated land cover is dominant. Unlike the surrogate model, which correctly identifies key drivers of recharge (e.g., precipitation, snow melt), XAI results from the stand-alone model identify some predictor variables that are correlated with simulated recharge (e.g., high slope and certain LULC classes) but don't physically drive recharge. These results highlight the effectiveness of ML surrogate models to meaningfully analyze physics-based simulation results. Stand-alone ML models may have high predictive accuracy but limited explanatory power in part due to the limited number of physically informative predictor variables that the model is trained on. The methods adopted in this study provide a valuable approach for investigating recharge dynamics in unconfined aquifers.

rows.title: An integrated vine-copula-based modeling framework for risk assessment and interval chance-constrained optimization of the water-energy-food nexus in a coastal watershed
rows.abstract: Agriculture is highly dependent on water and energy resources, while resource uncertainties and compound shortages increasingly challenge sustainable food production in watersheds. To address correlated resource risks in agricultural water–energy–food nexus (WEFN) systems, this study develops a vine-copula-based framework integrating joint-risk characterization, interval chance-constrained optimization, and multi-criteria scenario evaluation. The proposed framework represents water and agricultural energy as resource availability constraints and production inputs, with crop sown area as the primary decision variable. An entropy–AHP–TOPSIS approach was applied to evaluate representative scenarios. Application to the Jiulong River Basin, covering four administrative regions at an annual resolution from 2017 to 2023, considers 24 compound-risk scenarios. Results show that integrated system risk exceeds individual subsystem risks but remains below their sum. Increasing violation probability expands feasible allocation ranges and increases the lower-bound sown area by 2.4%. The framework provides risk-informed support for enhancing agricultural sustainability in coastal watersheds.

rows.title: UrbanFloodBench: Bridging AI and hydrology through benchmarking of coupled 1D–2D urban flood surrogate models
rows.abstract: Physics-based hydrodynamic models are the standard approach for urban flood simulation but remain computationally prohibitive for real-time modelling. Although machine learning surrogate models offer a promising alternative, most existing approaches rely on private or simplified datasets, limiting reproducibility and rigorous comparison, particularly for coupled 1D–2D flood systems. To address this gap, we introduce UrbanFloodBench, the first open benchmark for controlled coupled 1D–2D urban flood simulator emulation. UrbanFloodBench combines a multi-catchment HEC-RAS-derived dataset, a variance-aware evaluation framework, and a reproducible large-scale AI challenge. The Kaggle competition evaluated water-level prediction for two simplified, uncalibrated HEC-RAS benchmark catchments under spatially uniform synthetic rainfall, attracting 264 teams and 3799 submissions worldwide. Results show that multiple modelling approaches can achieve strong performance, while the 1D drainage component remains the primary unresolved challenge. UrbanFloodBench establishes a reproducible foundation for advancing AI-based surrogate modelling and future evaluation of data-driven flood-emulation methods.

rows.title: Integrated economic and environmental modeling of forest biomass for renewable energy in California: Statewide system implementation and application
rows.abstract: Planning forest biomass-to-energy systems requires integrating spatial resource data, supply chain logistics, technoeconomic modeling, and environmental impact assessment across large, heterogeneous landscapes. Existing tools typically address these components in isolation, limiting their ability to capture the coupled dynamics that determine project feasibility. Part I of this work introduced the Forest Resource and Renewable Energy Decision Support System (FRREDSS), which demonstrated the feasibility of web-based integrated assessment for the Sierra Nevada region. This paper presents FRREDSS 2.0, which extends that foundation with substantial new computational methods for statewide analysis, unifying six interlinked models within a scalable framework to evaluate forest biomass energy pathways across California. The system implements a two-stage cluster processing algorithm combining expanding-radius spatial search with cost-optimized greedy selection to solve annual feedstock procurement problems over 20-year planning horizons. A data transformation pipeline aggregates approximately 1 billion raster pixels from the C-BREC statewide biomass dataset into 2.1 million harvest clusters, each characterized by biomass availability, terrain attributes, and road access. Harvesting costs are computed via an enhanced Fuel Reduction Cost Simulator supporting 11 silvicultural treatments and 10 harvesting systems, and transportation distances are determined using the Open Source Routing Machine with a custom log-truck profile. Parallel execution of spatial queries and model computations achieves sub-second response times. A case study of a 25 MW facility in Butte County demonstrates the system’s ability to capture spatial depletion dynamics, with delivered feedstock costs rising from $42.50 to $133.35/BDT over the facility lifetime and a levelized cost of electricity of $142.72/MWh. FRREDSS 2.0 provides forest managers, energy developers, and policymakers with a unified platform for spatially explicit evaluation of biomass utilization strategies aligned with California’s renewable energy and forest resilience objectives.

rows.title: PatchX: A dual-branch embedding framework with cross-attention for streamflow forecasting
rows.abstract: Accurate streamflow forecasting is critical for flood management, yet hydrological models based on deep learning face an architectural dilemma: channel-mixing models may obscure heterogeneous hydrological signals through shared representations, while channel-independent architectures fail to explicitly capture causal rainfall-runoff mechanisms. We propose PatchX, a hydrologically structured dual-branch framework that separately encodes antecedent streamflow and meteorological information. This separation preserves runoff continuity while reducing interference from heterogeneous inputs. Multi-scale meteorological embeddings represent different response lags, and asymmetric cross-attention uses the runoff-state representation to select and incorporate relevant meteorological variables and temporal scales. Evaluated across six diverse basins (1- to 7-day lead times), PatchX consistently outperformed baselines, surpassing iTransformer and PatchTST by up to 7.82% and 3.78% in KGE. Furthermore, SHAP-based interpretability and ablation studies revealed that PatchX mitigates "attention collapse" and constructs internal mathematical representations that more closely align with physical and hydrological principles, providing a robust paradigm for streamflow forecasting.

rows.title: RCGAN: A generative adversarial framework for multi-variable bias correction in CMIP6 climate projections
rows.abstract: Climate model output carries systematic biases that limit its use in impact assessment, and conventional correction methods rest on statistical assumptions that constrain how nonlinear relationships are represented. This study evaluates the Residual Correction Generative Adversarial Network (RCGAN), developed in our previous work, for bias correction of relative humidity, precipitation and temperature from five CMIP6 models over China at monthly and daily resolution. Quantile Delta Mapping (QDM) and a CNN-based correction (CNNBC) serve as benchmarks, and all results refer to the 2006–2014 validation period. For monthly data, the relative improvement in Taylor Skill Score (TS) is approximately 77.8% for relative humidity, 26.7% for precipitation and 5.4% for temperature; the corresponding daily values are 114.9%, 26.1% and 9.5%. RCGAN attains a higher TS than QDM and CNNBC for relative humidity and precipitation, whereas for temperature it is only slightly better than either. The improvement therefore depends on the variable corrected.

rows.title: Editorial Board
KarstNSim 2.0: A pseudo-genetic method for comprehensive karst network simulation
rows.abstract: In this paper, we present KarstNSim 2.0, an upgraded version of the pseudo-genetic method and software KarstNSim for stochastic simulation of discrete karst networks in 3D. Leveraging recently acquired data and new karstogenetic studies on the Barrois Plateau in Meuse (France), our updated method now includes features to account for ghost-rock karstogenesis and model maze patterns with loops in the karst network topology. KarstNSim 2.0 also proposes to simulate the dimensions of conduits by incorporating karstology-driven spatial trends, ghost-rock influence and residual noise. KarstNSim 2.0 is demonstrated on the Barrois Plateau in Meuse, a large region with a complex history of polyphasic karstification, spanning over multiple spatio-temporal phases, each with their specific boundary conditions and karst morphologies. The realization consistency is ensured by a morphological comparison with real networks.

rows.title: Integrating MODIS and SMAP data for spatially calibrated SWAT+ modeling in a forested watershed of South Korea
rows.abstract: This study establishes a spatially, multi-variable calibrated SWAT + methodology integrating Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS) leaf area index (LAI) and evapotranspiration (ET) with Soil Moisture Active Passive (SMAP) soil moisture for the Yongdam Dam watershed, South Korea. Satellite datasets were aggregated by landscape units for parameter calibration and validation. The model reproduced spatial patterns of satellite observations (R2 > 0.94 for LAI, 0.80 for ET, 0.65 for soil moisture). While utilizing satellite products involves inherent data uncertainties, their integration significantly enhances the physical realism of the SWAT+. The satellite constrained calibration improved the representation of hydrograph dynamics more accurately than conventional calibration. Spatial calibration increased ET (+3.4%) and surface runoff (+1.8%) and decreased groundwater flow (−0.8%), revealing improved representation of surface water processes and energy–water interactions. The methodology demonstrates the utility of remote sensing integration in SWAT + to enhance spatial realism and reduce parameter equifinality.

rows.title: ParetoPick-R: An interactive tool for boosting the interpretability of multi-objective optimisation outputs
rows.abstract: This study presents ParetoPick-R, an R Shiny application for post-processing multi-objective optimisation (MOO) results in environmental modelling. Although MOO is widely used in environmental management, its multi-dimensional and abstract outputs are often hard to interpret and apply directly. ParetoPick-R addresses this challenge by enhancing the interpretability and usability of MOO results for decision support. The tool integrates three key strategies. First, interactive visualisation techniques enable users to explore synergies and trade-offs among objectives and link objective and decision spaces. Second, a clustering-based data reduction approach condenses large Pareto sets into representative subsets while preserving essential trade-off structures. Third, an Analytical Hierarchy Process facilitates the systematic incorporation of stakeholder preferences across objectives and decision variables. This paper describes the design and implementation of ParetoPick-R and demonstrates its functionality and procedural application through two distinct case studies.

rows.title: Temporal Inflow Dynamic Estimation Network (TideNet): A novel physics-informed graph neural network for daily reservoir inflow forecasting
rows.abstract: Forecasting river inflows remains a major challenge in hydrology due to the complexity of underlying physical processes, and existing deep learning models often fail to incorporate physical laws or capture hierarchical spatial dependencies. This study introduces TideNet, a physics-aware spatiotemporal forecasting framework that integrates Graph Neural Networks, Kolmogorov–Arnold Networks, Gated Recurrent Units, and Long Short-Term Memory modules. TideNet models the catchment as a dynamic graph in which edges encode slope-aware, hierarchical sub-catchment relationships, while KAN-based node updates capture nonlinear damping more effectively than multilayer perceptrons. Hydrological consistency is enforced through a mass-conserving message-passing mechanism, and 5-day-ahead inflows are predicted using an LSTM optimized with a custom AdaptiveFlow loss that prioritizes peak timing and magnitude. TideNet improves forecasting accuracy by 6% over leading spatiotemporal GNNs and 13% over temporal baselines, while remaining robust under sparse and noisy conditions, advancing physically consistent inflow forecasting for proactive flood management and climate-resilient reservoir operations.
